claim_policy.instructions: Check the linked issue and open pull requests before starting. Exclusive tasks should be claimed by issue comment or an early draft PR; parallel_ok tasks may have independent approaches but should avoid redundant scope.

tasks.title: Add automated live-link and source-durability checks
tasks.objective: Add a conservative validator that detects broken or clearly unstable source URLs without turning temporary network failures into false evidence failures.
tasks.why_it_matters: HumanityAI depends on traceable evidence, but current validators mostly verify structure rather than whether cited sources remain reachable and durable over time.
completion_criteria: Validator distinguishes hard failures from transient or rate-limited failures.
Known stable repository URLs do not trigger false failures in normal CI.
The workflow reports actionable diagnostics and does not silently delete or rewrite sources.
Tests cover at least success, permanent failure, redirect, and transient-failure behavior.
evidence_requirements: Use official HTTP status/redirect semantics and document failure policy.
Do not infer that a source is invalid from one transient network error.
tasks.notes: Prefer a warning or retry policy for ambiguous network failures; fail closed only on deterministic repository/schema errors.

tasks.title: Deepen baseline quality with complementary dimensions and contradiction checks
tasks.objective: First-pass indicator coverage now spans all top-level problem categories. Improve the weakest multidimensional baselines by adding only genuinely complementary indicators, newer or more global measurements, or credible contradictory estimates that change interpretation.
tasks.why_it_matters: One indicator per problem is enough for initial coverage but not for robust diagnosis. Several current records explicitly capture only one narrow dimension, so the next value comes from filling material measurement gaps rather than duplicating first-pass coverage.
completion_criteria: Name the existing indicator(s) for the selected problem and state the specific measurement gap the proposed record fills.
Each proposed indicator has an authoritative source, date/version, definition, limitations, and direct-versus-derived status.
Prefer a complementary dimension, materially newer/global measure, or credible contradictory estimate over a second indicator of the same construct.
Explain when no additional headline metric is defensible and preserve multidimensional measurement instead.
No composite ranking is introduced merely for convenience and duplicate or weaker indicators are not added.
evidence_requirements: Prefer primary official datasets, peer-reviewed sources, or major intergovernmental statistical systems.
Record material methodological controversy, uncertainty, and comparability limits.
Do not treat infrastructure, policy adoption, institutional existence, or inventory size as evidence of effectiveness or good outcomes.
tasks.notes: Initial coverage milestone is complete. High-value examples include job quality beyond the P07 jobs gap; rights/rule-of-law dimensions beyond P08 displacement/regime classification; wealth or opportunity inequality beyond P09 country Gini counts; information-integrity measures beyond P10 government trust; global/implementation dimensions beyond P14 EU strategy adoption; non-nuclear dimensions of P15; and coordination capacity beyond P16 online digital-ID availability. Parallel agents should choose different gaps.

tasks.title: Expand intervention-effectiveness evidence with strong negative and null results
tasks.objective: Add high-quality intervention evidence while deliberately searching for negative, null, heterogeneous, and replication-sensitive findings rather than only successful interventions.
tasks.why_it_matters: Resource discovery is not evidence of effectiveness; a useful prioritization system needs comparative outcome evidence and protection against publication or selection bias.
completion_criteria: Every added record identifies study design and population/context.
At least one credible negative, null, or materially qualifying finding is included when available.
Causal strength is not overstated beyond the underlying design.
Applicability limits and external-validity concerns are explicit.
evidence_requirements: Prefer systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized evaluations, strong quasi-experiments, or authoritative evidence syntheses.
Separate intervention evidence from organization/resource existence and from normative judgments.
tasks.notes: Parallel work is useful when agents cover different interventions or domains.

tasks.title: Independently reproduce and challenge HumanityAI quantitative claims
tasks.objective: Select existing quantitative claims or indicators and independently reproduce them from the cited source, documenting discrepancies, ambiguity, or hidden assumptions.
tasks.why_it_matters: Independent reproduction tests whether provenance is genuinely usable by outsiders and catches errors that structural schema validation cannot detect.
completion_criteria: The PR names the exact HumanityAI record IDs checked.
Each checked value is marked reproduced, qualified, corrected, or unresolved.
Any correction includes a source-grounded explanation rather than an unsupported replacement value.
No change is made when the original value is defensible; successful reproduction is still reported in the PR.
evidence_requirements: Use the original cited source or a more authoritative primary source when available.
Preserve uncertainty when source definitions or aggregation rules are ambiguous.
tasks.notes: This task is intentionally suitable for donated compute because independent replication has value even when no code change results.
